docs.title: About This Project
docs.text:
The College Document Archive System is a web-based document management system built with:

  • Python 3.13 + Flask 3.1.2
  • PostgreSQL 17.7 for data storage
  • Redis 7.4.7 for caching
  • Docker for containerization

Try it live: Open in GitHub Codespaces

Built with ❤️ and clean code

docs.title: Building a College Document Archive System: A Journey from Idea to Production
The Problem
docs.text:
I needed a document management system for a college to organize, track, and search administrative documents. The requirements were simple:

  • Upload and categorize documents
  • Search across content and metadata
  • Track activity with audit logs
  • Simple admin interface
  • No complex user management (single admin)

What started as a "simple Flask app" evolved into a complete production-ready system with modern tooling, containerization, and cloud deployment support.

docs.title: The Stack
docs.text: Component Technology Backend Python 3.13 + Flask 3.1.2 Database PostgreSQL 17.7 ORM SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Flask-SQLAlchemy Auth Flask-Login Cache Redis 7.4.7 Frontend Jinja2 + Custom CSS (Dark Theme) Container Docker + Docker Compose

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
1. Document Management
  2. Upload with auto-filename title detection
  3. Category organization (Admissions, Finance, HR, Academics)
  4. Academic period tracking (Fall/Spring/Summer by year)
  5. Tags for flexible labeling

  6. Automatic folder organization

  7. Search

  8. Full-text search across titles, content, descriptions

  9. PostgreSQL-powered search

  10. Admin Features

  11. Statistics dashboard
  12. Audit logging for all actions
  13. REST API for integrations
  14. Trash/restore functionality

docs.title: Phase 1: Bootstrap Defaults
docs.text: Started with Bootstrap 5, vanilla styling, light theme. Functional but generic.

docs.title: Phase 2: Custom Dark Theme
docs.text:
Midway through, I decided to create a distinctive look:

  • Fonts: Space Grotesk (display) + Spectral (body)
  • Colors: Deep black (#0a0a0a) with orange accent (#ff4d00)
  • Animations: Smooth transitions, hover effects
  • Layout: Fixed sidebar with responsive design

The result is a modern, professional interface that stands out from typical Bootstrap apps.

docs.title: Challenge 1: PostgreSQL Version Mismatch
docs.text:
When upgrading from PostgreSQL 15 to 17, the Docker container failed to start due to incompatible data directory.

Solution: - Removed old volumes with docker compose down -v - Fresh database initialization - Documented the issue for future reference

docs.title: Challenge 2: Python 3.14 Compatibility
docs.text:
Attempted to use Python 3.14 (latest), but many packages (psycopg2-binary, Pillow) lacked pre-built wheels.

Solution: - Downgraded to Python 3.13 (stable, all packages supported) - All dependencies work seamlessly

docs.title: Challenge 3: GitHub Codespaces 1-Click Experience
docs.text:
Initial devcontainer required Docker-in-Docker, which isn't enabled by default in Codespaces.

Solution: - Switched from PostgreSQL to SQLite for development - Removed Docker dependency from devcontainer - Added auto-start Flask command - True 1-click experience achieved

docs.title: Deployment Options Explored
docs.text:
Option Pros Cons Local (ngrok) Free, quick Exposes laptop, data usage GitHub Codespaces Cloud VM, 60hrs free Requires internet Railway Full Docker, managed DB $5/month after trial Render Good free tier Sleeps after 15min inactivity

Final choice: GitHub Codespaces for demos and development, with option to deploy to Railway for production.

docs.title: Lessons Learned
docs.text:
1. Start simple, iterate fast - Don't over-engineer early
  2. Containerization first - Docker from day one saved time
  3. Design matters - A distinctive UI makes projects memorable
  4. Test deployment early - Found issues before they became problems
  5. Document everything - README and comments help future you
